significance: A goddess temple on the bank of the Kalangi river at the southern edge of Sullurpeta, whose worship is traced to the fourth and fifth centuries and whose first built shrine, a small hut, is credited to the Cholas around the tenth century. The image is revered as Trikale Chengali, its left side read as Parvati, its right as Saraswati and its centre as Mahalakshmi.
